text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/donor-resolve-design-sol.md <<'EOF'
# Individual donor resolution design

Observed pipeline. Cleaning already emits person_name_normalized (title-free, punctuation-preserving, conservative parenthesized given-name unwrap). Resolution loads the funders schema but Observation ignores that column. Profiles currently group on generic normalized name and address. Native scorer creates candidates, then identity::classify decides eligibility, then component checks constrain unions. Attribution still checks generic name availability. Raw names, IDs, and cleaned artifact digests remain evidence.

Preferred minimal shape. Add person_name_normalized: Option<String> to Observation. Add one internal Observation method, individual_donor_name(&self) -> Option<&str>. It returns this field only when role is Donor and the existing identity::kind(self) == EntityKind::Person. Expose that existing classifier within the parent module or move it to a small shared identity evidence location; do not introduce a second Individual/person string list. Null/absent evidence returns None. Validate present person evidence against empty strings at the checked input boundary just as generic names are checked.

Keep generic profile names and profile grouping unchanged. Add a namespaced shared blocking key individual-donor-name:{name} using the method. This makes the candidates complete even when title or parenthesis differences defeat generic token blocking. Extend only the donor-name eligibility branch to accept either existing generic exact-name agreement or exact equality of two Some(individual_donor_name()) values. Reuse LinkEvidence::DonorName and existing component constraints/budget enforcement. This scopes the new equality to known person donors and leaves scorer feature semantics, organisation paths, unknown-kind donors, payer comparison and original evidence unchanged. Missing addresses remain allowed under the existing donor-name rule. Do not add fuzzy, initials, token-sort, accent-fold, surname-only, or person_core identity rules.

Why keep raw comparison profiles. The scorer remains the candidate producer and diagnostic probability owner. New shared blocking exposes candidates regardless of probability; classify already permits donor-name links without a probability threshold. Title-free matching is deterministic supporting evidence, not a fabricated statistical exact comparison. Do not replace generic exact_name globally, since that would extend title handling to the statistical/payer branch and can change grouping across kinds.

Alternative A, replace profile comparison name with title-free name. This yields exact scorer comparisons and groups donor variants but changes probability diagnostics/profile composition, and needs typed profile provenance to prevent unknown/org/payer observations borrowing the key. Larger scope without a necessary user benefit. Reject.

Alternative B, retain titles in the new key by reconstructing them around parenthesis-normalized remainder. This can join Lord (Michael) Farmer and Lord Michael Farmer but cannot join plain Michael Farmer. Adding both titled and title-free aliases duplicates matching policy. Reject for the requested title/plain equivalence. Retain titles only in raw evidence, not as identity requirements.

Consumer audit. Change Observation serde input and domain test constructors. funders_schema already includes the optional field and should stay unchanged. Profile grouping/scorer name remain unchanged; blocking gains one key. classify uses the same accessor as blocking. Components retain person/org and company-number conflict checks. Attribution name availability and payment resolution are untouched. Observation outcomes still use original normalized-name presence. Loader/public funder names and source raw parquet are untouched. Never infer donor kind from the parser, because person features are emitted for organisation-looking names too.

Regression. Prefer an isolated CLI integration test using the existing raw capture writer and command helper, not a mocked ScoredPairs fixture. Create separate occurrences for Lord Michael Farmer, Michael Farmer, Lord (Michael) Farmer and the corresponding Lord David Sainsbury, David Sainsbury, Lord (David) Sainsbury. Explicitly mark Individual, with at least one person spelling accepted by the existing classifier if useful. Invoke clean and real native resolve. Join cleaned funder_id to observation_resolution, assert six occurrences remain, exactly one non-null identity per expected donor, and different identity IDs across donors. Assert raw names unchanged and normalized person evidence exact. Preserve raw/cleaned files or compare bytes across resolve as existing test does. Add negative domain coverage showing the person key is absent for organisation, missing kind, payer and ultimate payer, and two different person names do not link. Add a blocking-level assertion that equivalent person evidence yields shared keys; this prevents reliance on incidental generic token blocking.

Demonstrate failure before consumer implementation by running the new full CLI regression against current resolution code with the completed cleaner. Then implement and rerun that same test with the native scorer. Keep candidate budget comfortably above fixture all-pair count so a budget refusal cannot masquerade as the intended identity failure. The expected initial failure is multiple identities within at least one donor family. No hardcoded production donor names.
EOF","max_output_tokens":1000}));

Saved design to [/tmp/donor-resolve-design-sol.md](/tmp/donor-resolve-design-sol.md).

Recommend consuming title-free person evidence through one donor/person-gated accessor, adding shared blocking keys, and extending existing donor-name identity eligibility. Keep scorer names, profile grouping, raw evidence, organisation rules, and payer matching unchanged.

Includes alternatives, consumer audit, and a real CLI regression plan with before/after verification.
